Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

You are an adversarial verifier. A finder claims this is LEGACY code safe to delete. Try hard to REFUTE it.

Finding: repo=andesim path=scripts/run_e2e.sh lines=7-9,25-31,36 kind=legacy-fallback
Claim: The bulk e2e runner still defaults VSIM_BUILD to the removed $ROOT/verilator/build and VSIM_QEMU to the removed $ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64 -- the QEMU default does not even consult QEMU_BIN_DIR, so it only works when setup.sh pre-exported VSIM_QEMU; the header comments document these dead defaults as current.
Evidence given: Line 27: VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}" (comment admits 'fall back to the legacy in-tree build only if it is unset'); line 31: VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}" with no ${QEMU_BIN_DIR} tier, unlike tests/lib/paths.sh:23. verilator/ removed by 1ad6667; in-tree QEMU build removed by daeca35. Comment line 36 still says engines sort 'under verilator/build/'.

Repo roots: andesim=/home/nick/work/andesim, vsim=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim.
Checks you MUST do:
1. Read the file/lines yourself — does the claim match reality?
2. grep BOTH repos (tracked files) for references: filename, function names, symbols, script names, make targets, cmake targets, doc links.
3. Check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/*, Makefiles, CMake, and CLAUDE.md/docs for indirect usage (variable-built names, glob patterns like test_*.sh runners).
4. git log --follow -5 on the file: was it recently touched for a live feature?
5. Is it an INTENTIONAL fallback/compat layer per CLAUDE.md (e.g. semihost_exit.inc)?
If ANY live reference or intentional-keep reason exists, verdict isLegacy=false. Default to false when uncertain. If true, give the exact deleteScope.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
3	# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
4	# workspace.
5	#
6	# Env overrides:
7	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
8	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
9	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
10	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
11	#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
12	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
13	#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
14	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
15	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
16	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
17	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
18	#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
19	#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
20	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
21	
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
25	# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
26	# VSIM_QEMU); fall back to the legacy in-tree build only if it is unset.
27	VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}"
28	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
29	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
30	
31	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
32	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
33	if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
34	  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
35	  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
36	  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
37	  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
38	  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
39	  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
40	  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
41	  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
42	    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
43	  fi
44	fi
45	
46	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
47	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
48	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
49	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
50	
51	require() {
52	  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
53	    fail "$1 not found: $2"
54	    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
55	    exit 1
56	  fi
57	}
58	require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
59	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
60	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
61	
62	export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN
63	
64	REQUIRED_ELFS=(
65	  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
66	  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
67	  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
68	  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
69	  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
70	)
71	need_build=0
72	for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
73	  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
74	done
75	if (( need_build )); then
76	  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
77	  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
78	fi
79	
80	# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified

1	# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
2	# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
3	#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
4	#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
5	#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
6	#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
7	#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
8	#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
9	#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
10	#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
11	#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
12	#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
13	
14	TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)
16	
17	if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
18	  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
19	fi
20	
21	hybrid_resolve_paths() {
22	  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
23	  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/build/qemu}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
24	  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
25	  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
26	  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
27	    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
28	      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
29	      exit 77
30	    fi
31	  done
32	}
33	
34	# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
35	# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
36	# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
37	hybrid_describe_int() {
38	  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
39	    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
40	}
41	
42	# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
43	# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
44	put_word_le() {
45	  local v=$3 bytes="" i
46	  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
47	    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
48	  done
49	  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
50	  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
51	}
52

117	# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
118	# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
119	# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
120	# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
121	# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
122	# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
123	# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
124	# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
125	SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
126	  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
127	  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"

130	MODE="${MODE:-both}"
131	case "$MODE" in
132	  marker|pc|both) ;;
133	  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;

136	default_jobs() {
137	  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
138	  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
139	  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
140	    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
141	    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
142	      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
143	      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
144	    fi
145	  fi
146	  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
147	  printf '%d\n' "$n"
148	}
149	JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
150	[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
151	  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
152	
153	FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
154	
155	LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
156	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
157	RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
158	LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
159	: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
160	: > "$LOCK_FILE"
161	
162	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
163	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
164	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
165	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
166	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
167	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
168	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
169	run_one() {
170	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
171	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
172	  local start end elapsed status rc
173	  start=$(date +%s)
174	  set +e
175	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
176	  rc=$?
177	  set -e
178	  end=$(date +%s)
179	  elapsed=$((end - start))
180	  case $rc in
181	    0)  status=PASS ;;
182	    77) status=SKIP ;;
183	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
184	  esac
185	  (
186	    flock 9
187	    case "$status" in
188	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
189	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
190	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
191	    esac
192	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
193	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
194	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
195	}
196	
197	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
198	# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
199	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
200	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
201	for tm in marker pc; do
202	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
203	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
204	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
205	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
206	    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
207	    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
208	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
209	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
210	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
211	  done
212	done
213	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
214	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
215	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
216	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
217	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
218	done
219	
220	# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
221	# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
222	declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
223	for tm in marker pc; do
224	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
225	  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
226	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
227	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
228	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
229	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
230	    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
231	  done
232	done
233	
234	TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
235	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
236	
237	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
238	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
239	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
240	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
241	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
242	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
243	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
244	mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
245	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
246	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
247	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
248	  printf '.\n' >&8
249	done
250	
251	i=0
252	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
253	  i=$((i+1))
254	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
255	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
256	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
257	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
258	  read -r -u 8 _tok
259	  (
260	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
261	    printf '.\n' >&8
262	  ) &
263	done
264	wait
265	exec 8>&-
266	
267	# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
268	for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
269	  i=$((i+1))
270	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
271	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
272	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
273	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
274	  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
275	done
276	
277	declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
278	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
279	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
280	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
281	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
282	  case "$r_status" in
283	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
284	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
285	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
286	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
287	  esac
288	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
289	
290	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
291	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
292	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
293	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
294	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
295	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
296	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
297	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
298	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
299	    echo
300	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
301	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
302	  fi
303	done
304	
305	echo
306	marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
307	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
308	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
309	total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
310	total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
311	total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
312	step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
313	if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
314	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
315	  exit 1
316	fi
317

The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. # test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that

#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):

#

#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}
